memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If a man has two wives, and he loves one but not the other, and both bear him sons but the firstborn is the son of the wife he does not love, when he wills his property to his sons, he must not give the rights of the firstborn to the son of the wife he loves in preference to his actual firstborn, the son of the wife he does not love. - Deut 21:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This law addresses a painful family situation. In a household with two wives, a father might be tempted to favour the son of the wife he loved more, and cheat the true firstborn out of his rightful inheritance. God forbids this. Justice was not to be twisted by favouritism. The firstborn's rights could not be stolen simply because his mother was less loved.

We should note that God is not endorsing polygamy here, which consistently brought pain and division in Scripture, as we see in families like Jacob's. Rather, God is protecting the vulnerable within a broken situation, ensuring that a child was not robbed because of his parent's favouritism. God cares about fairness even in messy, imperfect family circumstances.

Favouritism is a poison that damages families, and God stands against it. He calls His people to treat others justly, not according to our personal preferences or affections, but according to what is right. This challenges us wherever we are tempted to favour some people over others unfairly, in our families, workplaces, or churches. Scripture is clear that God shows no favouritism, and neither should we (Jas 2:1). Our God deals with each of us justly and lovingly, never playing favourites in a way that wrongs anyone. Where might favouritism be creeping into the way you treat the people around you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might favouritism be shaping how you treat others?
2. How does God's impartial justice challenge you?
3. Who around you needs to be treated more fairly?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You show no favouritism and deal justly with all. Root out any favouritism in me and help me treat everyone fairly. Amen.
